research_question: What is the effect of rituximab compared with tacrolimus on relapse by 12 months in children with steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome?
outcome_description: Nephrotic syndrome relapse by 12 months of follow-up
positive_direction: A positive effect size favors rituximab over tacrolimus (indicating a lower risk or rate of relapse by 12 months in the rituximab group).
search_queries: rituximab tacrolimus pediatric nephrotic syndrome relapse trial
rituximab versus tacrolimus steroid sensitive nephrotic syndrome comparison
rituximab tacrolimus childhood nephrotic syndrome randomized controlled
inclusion_criteria: Studies examining children and adolescents with steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome (including frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent courses).
Comparative studies evaluating rituximab versus tacrolimus.
Reporting quantitative data on disease relapse or relapse-free status by 12 months of follow-up.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, letters, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No direct comparison between a rituximab arm and a tacrolimus arm.
No quantitative outcome data on relapse by 12 months that can produce an effect size (e.g., event counts and total randomized per arm, risk ratios, or odds ratios).
Completely unrelated to pediatric steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome.
moderators_to_extract: Nephrotic syndrome subtype (frequently relapsing vs steroid-dependent)
Rituximab dosing regimen (single infusion vs multiple/repeated infusions)
Concomitant maintenance immunosuppression or steroid taper protocol
Study design (randomized controlled trial vs non-randomized prospective trial)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) comparing the proportion of patients experiencing relapse by 12 months between rituximab and tacrolimus groups.
